info.title: uqf frontend API
info.summary: Validated, parameterised access to the uqf TorQ gateway

get.description:
Who the caller is, their groups, and every (feature, action) the
access policy grants them (#2045). The browser shows and hides views
from it; the server enforces the same policy on every route, so
nothing here is a promise the UI keeps on its own.
Pending and running queries on the gateway.
Which backend handles the gateway has, and who is connected.

Fleet-wide query log, assembled here because none exists in q.

`unreachable` is part of the response rather than an error: one process
being down must not blank the view for the other nine.

Every client connected to any process in the fleet.

Distinct from `/ops/connections`, which reports the GATEWAY's clients.
A process that connects to the tickerplant rather than the gateway
does not appear there at all — which is the whole reason this exists.

The motivating case is the cryptorust recorder: it opens an outbound
connection to `stp1` and never listens, so it cannot be a TorQ
discovery member, and registering it as one would put a permanently
unreachable row in the fleet view. TorQ already tracks it here, in
`.clients.clients` of the process it connects to. See
docs/architecture/cryptorust-discovery.md.

Reuses UsageResponse: the shape is the same fleet-wide-merge-plus-
unreachable, and a second identical model would be two places for one
idea.

Fleet health for every process process.csv declares - or, in a
target's workspace, every process its release declares, probed
through the forwards uqs holds open.

Liveness comes from an IPC probe rather than OS process inspection,
so the same mechanism works whether or not the process is on this
machine - see health.py for why that matters.

Backfill and Airflow task status, read from the files q writes.

Read from disk rather than from the gateway because q writes these
and nothing publishes them over IPC. Carries only q's own facts -
see status.py on the authority boundary this deliberately does not cross.

Every workspace a request may name: `local` and each target the
uqs registry declares, read as /services reads it - no server is
contacted. Which one a request reads is the request's own header.

The workspace this request names, reached now: for a target, the
connection uqs holds open and each process's forward. A target that
cannot be reached is an error naming it - never the local answer.

The deployment targets this machine declares, as `uqs target list
--json` reads them: from deploy_targets.toml and the local deploy
history, with no ssh - see services.py.

List one directory under a registered target's deployment root,
over ssh, with the release's own Python - see remote_files.py.

Reads only. Behind the authz guard like every route, and it reaches a
server with this machine's ssh key, so it needs remote operations on
(UQF_FRONTEND_ENABLE_WRITES) and, through the write guard, the token.

put.description:
Write the request body to `path` below a registered target's
shared/config, over ssh, with the release's own Python - see
remote_files.upload (#1951).

Refuses before reading the body when writes are off, the path is
unsafe or outside shared/config, the target is not registered, or
Content-Length is over the limit; refuses a body that grows past it
while read. An existing file is replaced only with `overwrite=true`.
A timeout or lost answer is 504 UploadOutcomeUncertain, never retried.
`push_id` is the push this file belongs to (POST .../config/pushes):
the server keeps what it replaces, and what it wrote, in that push's
history (#2002).

get.description:
The target's tunnel plan, as `uqs target tunnel plan --json` makes
it: processes and ports from its release, each mapping's state from the
last check. Opens no tunnel - see tunnels.py.

Each mapping checked layer by layer, as `uqs target tunnel check
--json` does: a failed endpoint never hides a healthy one.

Composed coverage for one dataset, coverage slice and source
release, plus the gaps in a requested range if one is given.

`slice` has no default on purpose. FastAPI makes a parameter with
no default REQUIRED, so omitting it is a 422 naming the field rather
than a plausible answer computed across every slice (#185). Pass
`""` for a dataset with no slice dimension.

The range is both bounds or neither (#2222), as on every route that
names a coverage window: one bound alone was parsed and then dropped,
answering 200 with no gaps for a question that was never asked.

parameters.name: slice

schema.description: the coverage slice to read; "" for a dataset with no slice dimension
schema.title: Slice

parameters.description: the coverage slice to read; "" for a dataset with no slice dimension

get.description: Every prepared chart and the schema of its parameters (#2044).

post.description:
One prepared chart's figure. The body is validated against the
chart's own schema; it reads only through the chart's vetted query
(charts.py), and a table it reads is put to the policy like /query's.

One or more tables on two endpoints - this stack (`local`) or a
registered target - over an explicit window, as `uqs data diff --json`
compares them (compare.py). Each table must be one this stack's
catalog lists, and is put to the policy, like /query's; each side is
read to at most max_rows. A target side is held to what /services/{target}/... is,
since only the body names it (#2066): the write token while writes
are on (the middleware's gates - by path, and `_reaches_target`'s by
header on scoped routes, #2067 - cannot see a side named in the body),
services:read, and remote operations, as it is reached over ssh with
the operator's key. The Host check ran in the middleware already.

Open a push when the operator confirms it: one id for all its
uploads, and its history on the server. Retention prunes old pushes
here, each audited.

get.description: A target's config pushes, newest first, from the server's history.

post.description:
Close a push: the `config.push` summary row - config_dir, file
count, bytes and one outcome per file, from the server's own record
where it has one and the browser's report where it never got one.

get.description: One push: each file's action, hashes and what it is now.

Before against after, fetched from the server's history on demand:
text under the cap, sizes and hashes for anything else. Not audited -
a read - and so its text never reaches the activity store.
What restoring the push would do - a dry run, writing nothing.

post.description:
Put a push's files back as they were before it - deleting those it
created - as a confirmed push of its own. Refused, writing nothing,
when a file changed since; a lost answer is uncertain, never retried.

get.description:
Whether writes are on, and what can be set.

A GET, and deliberately not itself gated: a UI needs to know whether
to render controls at all, and making it discover that by provoking a
403 on a real action is a poor way to find out.

post.description: Start, stop or restart processes (action is start|stop|restart).

put.description: Persist one process.csv field override, applied on the next start.
Set a `.qetl.cfg` override in the live process the gateway addresses.

post.description: Launch a bounded worker over a range. Detached; watch /ops/backfill.

What an operator did in the UI. Intent, as the browser reports it -
the server's own rows are the authority on what happened. Written in
one transaction, and with it the count of what the browser could not
send. Without the write token, rate-limited (#2019).

get.description:
The history, newest first, filtered; whether it is being kept, how
much of each level is, and what was not. `level` is the most
detailed level shown: `interactions` shows actions too.

The history as a file: JSON Lines, CSV, or a timeline a person
reads (activity_export.render) - oldest first, under the same filters as
GET /activity, at most activity_log.EXPORT_MAX events. Cut at the
limit, it says so: a header line in text, and X-UQF-Truncated.

The policy and runtime settings, the secrets' presence, and the
schemas the browser builds its forms from.

put.description: Replace the access policy - see the module docstring for every check.

Replace the runtime settings - in force at once, kept in
UQF_FRONTEND_SETTINGS_FILE for the next start.

AccessChangeRequest.title: AccessChangeRequest
AccessChangeRequest.description:
PUT /settings/access: the whole new policy, and the version it was
edited from - a change made since is refused, not overwritten.

AccessPolicyBody.title: Access policy
AccessPolicyBody.description: The whole access policy: who may do what, and who is in which group.

ActivityBatchRequest.title: ActivityBatchRequest
ActivityBatchRequest.description:
What the browser sends: a batch, so navigation does not cost a request
each - and what it could not send, so nothing is lost without a number.

ActivityBound.title: ActivityBound
ActivityBound.description: How much of one level is kept: the tighter of the two wins.

ActivityDrop.title: ActivityDrop
ActivityDrop.description: Events not in the history, by level and why, since the file began.

ActivityEventOut.title: ActivityEventOut
ActivityEventOut.description:
One stored event. `claimed_user` is the x-uqf-user header as sent: a
label, never an authenticated identity.

ActivityItem.title: ActivityItem
ActivityItem.description: One item's outcome, for an action over several things.

ActivityPersistence.title: ActivityPersistence
ActivityPersistence.description: Whether history is being kept, and whether writes have failed.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: more events matched than were returned: `limit` cut them (#2220)

ActivityResponse.title: ActivityResponse
ActivityResponse.description: The history, newest first, with how it is kept and what it lost.

range_to.title: Range To
range_to.description: ISO-8601 with an explicit offset, exclusive

BackfillRequest.title: BackfillRequest
BackfillRequest.description:
Run a bounded worker over a range.

Every field is required and none has a default. The explicit-range rule at the HTTP
surface: a backfill that guessed a range would publish the wrong window
and record it as covered.

BackfillStartedResponse.title: BackfillStartedResponse
BackfillStartedResponse.description:
Launched, not finished.

The run is detached, so this says what was started and where to watch it
rather than whether it worked - `/ops/backfill` reads the status file the
worker writes on every transition.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: `failed` is counted separately from `running`, since a worker still in flight is not a problem

unreadable.title: Unreadable
unreadable.description: Files present but not parseable. Reported rather than raised, so one damaged file cannot hide every healthy worker

BackfillStatusResponse.title: BackfillStatusResponse
BackfillStatusResponse.description:
What q reports about its own backfill runs.

Carries only facts q owns under the authority split - startup, source reads, failures,
checkpoints, run and window counts. Airflow's facts (task ordering,
retries, timeouts, concurrency) are deliberately absent: inferring them
from these files is the cross-layer inference the authority split forbids.

BrowserDropIn.title: BrowserDropIn
BrowserDropIn.description:
Events the browser did not send, counted: sampled by debug's rate
limit, or pushed out of its queue while the API was unreachable.

BrowserEventIn.title: BrowserEventIn
BrowserEventIn.description:
One thing an operator did in the UI.

Strict, and every field bounded: `detail` keys outside
activity.DETAIL_KEYS are dropped before anything is stored, and there is
no field for a typed value, a token or a file's contents.

CapabilitiesResponse.title: CapabilitiesResponse
CapabilitiesResponse.description:
GET /me/capabilities (#2045): who the caller is, as far as a trusted
proxy vouches, and what the access policy lets them do. The browser hides
or disables what is not here; the server refuses it either way.

Capability.title: Capability
Capability.description: One (feature, action) the access policy grants (access.py).

CatalogResponse.title: CatalogResponse
CatalogResponse.description:
The queryable surface, so a UI can build filter controls from the
server's own whitelist rather than hardcoding a copy that drifts.

point_limit.title: Point Limit
point_limit.description: the most points its figure carries

params.title: Params
params.description: the JSON Schema its request body must validate against

ChartInfo.title: ChartInfo
ChartInfo.description: One prepared chart, as GET /charts lists it (charts.py, #2044).

point_limit.title: Point Limit
point_limit.description: the most points this chart's figure may carry

downsampled.title: Downsampled
downsampled.description: a series was reduced (LTTB) to fit point_limit

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: the read was cut at a row cap, or series were left out to fit point_limit

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: what was left out, and why, in words

ChartResponse.title: ChartResponse
ChartResponse.description: One drawn chart: a plotly.py figure, and what was done to fit it.

decimals.title: Decimals
decimals.description: Decimal places this column is shown with, resolved from the column, then its table, then its type. None means show the value as it arrives - a symbol, a boolean, or a count that has no fractional part

CommandResponse.title: CommandResponse
CommandResponse.description:
What a subprocess-backed control action did.

Carries the exit code rather than only a boolean: torq.sh distinguishes
"nothing to do" from "failed", and collapsing that to ok/not-ok loses the
distinction an operator acts on.

checked.title: Checked
checked.description: false when no source_version was given

gaps.title: Gaps
gaps.description: what of the window this side has not published

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: {column, op, value} objects with /catalog's operators, as on /query

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: rows read per side, at most

source_version.title: Source Version
source_version.description: the release whose coverage to compare; null compares no coverage

slice.title: Slice
slice.description: the coverage slice, required with source_version; "" for a dataset with no slice dimension

CompareRequest.title: CompareRequest
CompareRequest.description: POST /compare: two explicit sides, an explicit window, filters and a row limit.

ok.title: Ok
ok.description: true only when every table is equal_in_sample

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: the filters as they were sent

source_version.title: Source Version
source_version.description: null when no coverage was compared

slice.title: Slice
slice.description: the coverage slice compared; null when no coverage was compared

left.title: Left
left.description: the type on the left, or "absent"

right.title: Right
right.description: the type on the right, or "absent"

label.title: Label
label.description: what the outcome means here; a truncated sample says so

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: a side stopped at the row limit: a sample, not the table

read.title: Read
read.description: rows read on the left and on the right

unpaired.title: Unpaired
unpaired.description: keys one truncated sample holds alone, not judged

CompareTable.title: CompareTable
CompareTable.description: One table's verdict, as q decided it.

ConfigDiffFileOut.title: ConfigDiffFileOut
ConfigDiffFileOut.description:
Before against after for one file: `text` carries a unified diff; a
`binary`, `oversized` or `omitted` (past the answer's cap) file only its
sizes and sha256s.

dest.title: Dest
dest.description: the target's deployment root: its registry `dest`, without a trailing /

diff_cap.title: Diff Cap
diff_cap.description: the largest file diffed as text, in bytes

dest.title: Dest
dest.description: the target's deployment root: its registry `dest`, without a trailing /

ConfigPushFileOut.title: ConfigPushFileOut
ConfigPushFileOut.description:
One file of a push, from its manifest: what it did, the hashes before
and after, and - when read with `show` - what the file is now.

confirmed.title: Confirmed
confirmed.description: must be true: the operator confirmed it

config_dir.title: Config Dir
config_dir.description: the directory pushed to, relative to dest

ConfigPushOpenRequest.title: ConfigPushOpenRequest
ConfigPushOpenRequest.description:
POST /services/{target}/config/pushes: what the operator confirmed -
the uploads overwrite server config, so `confirmed` is required (#2244).

dest.title: Dest
dest.description: the target's deployment root: its registry `dest`, without a trailing /

push_id.title: Push Id
push_id.description: every upload of this push names it

max_kept.title: Max Kept
max_kept.description: the newest pushes the history keeps

retention_days.title: Retention Days
retention_days.description: the days the history keeps a push

ConfigPushReported.title: ConfigPushReported
ConfigPushReported.description: A file the browser sent - or did not - that the server never recorded.

dest.title: Dest
dest.description: the target's deployment root: its registry `dest`, without a trailing /

reported_count.title: Reported Count
reported_count.description: files the browser reported; `push.reported` lists them

ConfigPushSummaryOut.title: ConfigPushSummaryOut
ConfigPushSummaryOut.description:
One push in a target's history. `error` when its manifest could not
be read; the other fields are then null.

confirmed.title: Confirmed
confirmed.description: must be true: the operator confirmed it

dest.title: Dest
dest.description: the target's deployment root: its registry `dest`, without a trailing /

restores.title: Restores
restores.description: the push this restore undoes, as its manifest names it

ConfigRestoreResponse.title: ConfigRestoreResponse
ConfigRestoreResponse.description:
A restore's plan (GET) or what it did (POST): the restore is a push
of its own, `push_id`, so it can be restored in turn.

start_with_all.title: Start With All
start_with_all.description: whether torq.sh's "all" selector includes it - the effective value, with process_overrides.csv applied

ControlProcessOut.title: ControlProcessOut
ControlProcessOut.description: One process a lifecycle selector may name.

processes.title: Processes
processes.description: what a lifecycle selector may name, from the effective process.csv; empty while writes are off, like settable_fields

ControlStatusResponse.title: ControlStatusResponse
ControlStatusResponse.description:
Whether the control surface is live, and what it accepts.

A UI needs this to decide whether to render controls at all. Discovering
it by provoking a 403 on a real action is a poor way to find out, and on
a lifecycle route the "real action" would have stopped the fleet.

slice.title: Slice
slice.description: the coverage slice to check; "" for a dataset with no slice dimension

range_to.title: Range To
range_to.description: ISO-8601 with an explicit offset, exclusive

CoverageRequirement.title: CoverageRequirement
CoverageRequirement.description:
An opt-in pre-check: refuse the query unless this range is published.

``source_version`` is mandatory, not optional, because the framework requires
coverage consumers to filter on it - coverage under one source release
says nothing about another.

``slice`` is mandatory for the same reason and is NOT ``min_length=1``:
the empty string is the legitimate "this dataset has no slice
dimension" sentinel, which q records as the null symbol. Requiring the
field while allowing it to be empty is the distinction that matters - the
caller must say which slice they mean, and "the whole dataset" is one of
the things they can say, but silence is not (#185).

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: True when the requested range has no gaps

CoverageResponse.title: CoverageResponse
CoverageResponse.description: Composed coverage and any gaps, for one dataset at one source release.

DeployedOut.title: DeployedOut
DeployedOut.description: The release last deployed to a target from this workstation.

Filter.title: Filter
Filter.description:
One validated predicate. ``value`` stays ``Any`` here on purpose: the
real type check happens in :func:`uqf_frontend.queries.coerce`, against
the column's declared q type, which pydantic cannot know.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: down_unexpected excludes processes with startwithall=0, since those being down is configured behaviour rather than a fault

InspectionOut.title: InspectionOut
InspectionOut.description: Inspection mode as the server enforces it (inspection.py, #2032).

LifecycleRequest.title: LifecycleRequest
LifecycleRequest.description:
Start, stop or restart processes.

`procs` is torq.sh's own selector - a name, several separated by spaces,
or "all" - and is passed through rather than reinterpreted, so the HTTP
surface and the CLI cannot disagree about what "all" means.

Required, with no default (#1361): it defaulted to "all", so a body that
lost the field - renamed on the browser's side - made Stop stop the whole
fleet. A destructive action is never what silence means.

OpsTableResponse.title: OpsTableResponse
OpsTableResponse.description:
A raw operational table, plus the cadence the UI should poll it at.

The cadence is advisory and served rather than hardcoded in the client,
because polling is the only mechanism and the right interval
depends on how fast the underlying state moves.

subject.title: Who
subject.description: A user, a group, `anonymous` (a caller no proxy vouched for), or * for everyone

feature.title: Feature
feature.description: A view, or * for every one

value.title: Value
value.description: the new value; "" is legal and clears nothing

ProcessConfigRequest.title: ProcessConfigRequest
ProcessConfigRequest.description:
One process.csv field override.

`field` because it names a COLUMN of process.csv, one of
ControlStatusResponse.settable_fields; WorkerConfigRequest's `key` names a
`.qetl.cfg` KEY in a live process. Two stores, two words (#2227).

ProcessConfigResponse.title: ProcessConfigResponse
ProcessConfigResponse.description:
The effective row after the write.

The row rather than an acknowledgement: what the process will start with
is the interesting part, and a caller who must issue a second request to
learn it will sometimes not bother.

identity_mismatch.title: Identity Mismatch
identity_mismatch.description: Set when the process answering that port is not the one process.csv declares there - a stale process squatting a port looks healthy to any check that only asks whether something is listening

ProcessHealthOut.title: ProcessHealthOut
ProcessHealthOut.description:
One row of /ops/processes. The process's type is `proctype`, TorQ's
column, and only that: a `group` field repeated it under a word that means
an access group elsewhere (#2232).

PrunedPushOut.title: PrunedPushOut
PrunedPushOut.description: A push whose history retention removed.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: rows to return; cut at the server's max_rows, reported as `truncated`

tier.title: Tier
tier.description: rdb = today's session, hdb = completed partitions, both = razed. hdb is expected to be slower

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: more rows existed than were returned, whatever cut them (#2220)

cut_by.title: Cut By
cut_by.description: what cut a truncated result: the caller's `limit`, or a server row cap - UQF_FRONTEND_MAX_ROWS or the query policy's maxrows (#928, #1255); null when nothing did

report_error.title: Report Error
report_error.description: why the report was not read

ReleaseOut.title: ReleaseOut
ReleaseOut.description:
What the target's `current` names, read as a link and never followed,
and the fields of that release's deploy-report.json worth showing.

confirmed.title: Confirmed
confirmed.description: must be true: the operator confirmed it

dest.title: Dest
dest.description: the target's deployment root: its registry `dest`, without a trailing /

mtime.title: Mtime
mtime.description: last modified, UTC to the nanosecond

RemoteEntryOut.title: RemoteEntryOut
RemoteEntryOut.description:
One entry of a remote directory (remote_helper.describe). A symlink,
special file or undecodable name is `blocked`: listed, never entered.

dest.title: Dest
dest.description: the target's deployment root: its registry `dest`, without a trailing /

path.title: Path
path.description: the directory listed, relative to the root; empty is the root

parent.title: Parent
parent.description: the parent directory's path; null at the root

total.title: Total
total.description: entries in the directory; null when too many to count

RemoteFilesResponse.title: RemoteFilesResponse
RemoteFilesResponse.description: GET /services/{target}/files: one directory under a deployment root.

dest.title: Dest
dest.description: the target's deployment root: its registry `dest`, without a trailing /

path.title: Path
path.description: the file written, relative to the root

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: of the bytes written, as the server checked them

replaced.title: Replaced
replaced.description: an existing file was replaced (overwrite was asked)

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: the file's permission bits; a replaced file's are kept

created_dirs.title: Created Dirs
created_dirs.description: directories created on the way, relative to the root

push_id.title: Push Id
push_id.description: the push this file belongs to (#2002)

previous_size.title: Previous Size
previous_size.description: bytes of the file replaced; null on create

previous_sha256.title: Previous Sha256
previous_sha256.description: sha256 of the file replaced, kept in the push history; null on create

RemoteUploadResponse.title: RemoteUploadResponse
RemoteUploadResponse.description:
PUT /services/{target}/files: one file written below the
target's shared/config, published in one atomic step (#1951).

RestoreStepOut.title: RestoreStepOut
RestoreStepOut.description:
What restoring one file takes: write its before content back, delete
the file the push created, nothing, or - changed since - a conflict.

RuntimeChangeRequest.title: RuntimeChangeRequest
RuntimeChangeRequest.description: PUT /settings/runtime: every runtime setting, and the version.

activity_level.title: Default activity level
activity_level.description: What a browser tab records unless its operator picks another; the server audits every change whatever this says

RuntimeSettingsBody.title: Runtime settings
RuntimeSettingsBody.description:
The frontend's settings that take effect without a restart - and
only those. A setting that holds a secret is never one of them.

SecretSetting.title: SecretSetting
SecretSetting.description:
A setting that holds a secret: whether it is set, and never its value.
Not editable here - it is set in the server's environment.

ssh.title: Ssh
ssh.description: the ssh destination, user@host - never contacted to list it

dest.title: Dest
dest.description: the deployment root on that server

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: the [environments.NAME] layer the target names, if any

inspection.title: Inspection
inspection.description: in inspection mode: the API and uqs refuse every write to it (#2032)

last_deployed.description: from this workstation's deploy_history.json, not from the server

ServiceTargetOut.title: ServiceTargetOut
ServiceTargetOut.description:
One deployment target, as `uqs target list --json` lists it: the same
keys (#2107).

source.title: Source
source.description: the deploy_targets.toml that was read, or would be

writes_enabled.title: Writes Enabled
writes_enabled.description: whether an action reaching a server could run here: UQF_FRONTEND_ENABLE_WRITES, with its token. Listing never reaches one

ServicesResponse.title: ServicesResponse
ServicesResponse.description:
The deployment targets this machine declares (services.py).

`invalid` carries the registry's refusal, naming the line, when the file
exists but cannot be read: reported rather than raised, so the view can
show the file and the reason together.

SettingChange.title: SettingChange
SettingChange.description: One line of a change's diff, as it is audited.

SettingsChangeResponse.title: SettingsChangeResponse
SettingsChangeResponse.description: What a change did: its diff, as audited, and the new version.

SettingsResponse.title: SettingsResponse
SettingsResponse.description:
GET /settings: what the caller may see of the frontend's settings,
each part with the JSON schema its form is rendered from.

TunnelCheckRecordOut.title: TunnelCheckRecordOut
TunnelCheckRecordOut.description: A mapping's last successful check, as `uqs target tunnel check` recorded it.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: every category, and what it means

TunnelCheckResponse.title: TunnelCheckResponse
TunnelCheckResponse.description:
GET /services/{target}/tunnel/check: `uqs target tunnel check --json`.
`category` and `error` are set when no endpoint could be checked.

category.title: Category
category.description: None when it passed, else the first failing layer's category - a key of `categories`, as the response's own `category`

layers.title: Layers
layers.description: each layer: ok, failed or skipped

connected.title: Connected
connected.description: the planned local port already serves this process

reported_process.title: Reported Process
reported_process.description: the process the port answered as, when it answered - ProcessHealthOut.reported_process's name for the same fact (#2236)

TunnelEndpointOut.title: TunnelEndpointOut
TunnelEndpointOut.description: One endpoint of a tunnel check (uqs.deploy.tunnel_check).

local_endpoint.title: Local Endpoint
local_endpoint.description: host:port on this machine, once the tunnel is open

query_command.title: Query Command
query_command.description: a uqs command querying it from here, no credential

state.title: State
state.description: verified: a check in the last hour proved these ports; stale: proved longer ago or for other ports; unverified: never proved

last_success.description: the last check that proved this mapping; a failure never writes it

listening.title: Listening
listening.description: something accepts on the local port now - a hint, not proof

TunnelMappingOut.title: TunnelMappingOut
TunnelMappingOut.description:
One forward of a tunnel plan (uqs.deploy.tunnel_plan): configured,
and - separately - what its last check proved.

launch_command.title: Launch Command
launch_command.description: the ssh opening every forward; no credential

available.title: Available
available.description: forwardable processes the plan did not select

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: more rows existed than were returned: `limit` cut them (#2220)

unreachable.title: Unreachable
unreachable.description: Processes that could not be reached. Reported rather than raised, so one process being down does not blank the whole view

processes_configured.title: Processes Configured
processes_configured.description: 0 means nothing is configured to fan out to - an empty log here means unconfigured, not an idle fleet

UsageResponse.title: UsageResponse
UsageResponse.description: The fleet-wide query log that q itself does not provide.

WorkerConfigRequest.title: WorkerConfigRequest
WorkerConfigRequest.description:
One `.qetl.cfg` override, set in a live process. `key` is a
`.qetl.cfg` key, not a process.csv column - ProcessConfigRequest's `field`.

note.title: Note
note.default: this override lives in the process's memory and is lost when it restarts; a process.csv override survives

WorkerConfigResponse.title: WorkerConfigResponse
WorkerConfigResponse.description:
Where the value now comes from.

`explain` names the LAYER that answered, which is not always the override
just written - a key also set in the environment reads from there. A
caller told only "ok" would believe a value that is not in effect.

reactions_owed.title: Reactions Owed
reactions_owed.description: reactions to this run's publications that have not succeeded - a derived dataset is stale

abandoned.title: Abandoned
abandoned.description: not terminal, and its process is gone - it will never record an outcome

WorkspaceEndpointOut.title: WorkspaceEndpointOut
WorkspaceEndpointOut.description: One of a target's processes, as this API reaches it.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: how this API reaches it: its own stack directly, or a target through the ssh forwards uqs opens

access.title: Access
access.description: what the workspace allows: a target is read-only - control acts on this API's own stack only

ssh.title: Ssh
ssh.description: the target's ssh destination; never contacted to list

available.title: Available
available.description: whether it can be selected here: a target needs remote operations

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: why it cannot be selected, when it cannot

WorkspaceOut.title: WorkspaceOut
WorkspaceOut.description:
One workspace the browser may select (#2029): `local`, this API's own
stack, or a target the uqs registry declares (workspaces.py). `target`
as in WorkspaceResponse and the x-uqf-target header: `local` is a name
the registry reserves (#2107).

ssh.title: Ssh
ssh.description: the target's ssh destination; None for local

WorkspaceResponse.title: WorkspaceResponse
WorkspaceResponse.description: The workspace a request named, reached: proof it is available now.

header.title: Header
header.description: the request header that names a request's workspace

source.title: Source
source.description: the deploy_targets.toml that was read, or would be

WorkspacesResponse.title: WorkspacesResponse
WorkspacesResponse.description:
Every workspace, from the uqs target registry plus `local`. No server
is contacted to list them, and the browser keeps no registry of its own.
